clue.text: Blue oval roof constructed? It's not done for gain

indicators.note: something constructed is built up from parts, so these three words' letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A question about a blue oval roof being built, as though from an architect's sketchbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed?' signals rearranging the letters of BLUE OVAL ROOF; the question mark covers the surface sense, and the definition is the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes work undertaken purely for pleasure or devotion, with no payment expected.

clue.text: Brief of those not ministers to restrain right winger

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the lay word holds the politician within it

parts.note: laic means relating to the laity, people who are not clergy
Con is short for a Conservative, a politician on the right

explanation.surface: Reads as a terse summary of how lay people keep a right-wing politician in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' here are clergy, not government members, which misleads the political surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief, terse way of speaking uses few words, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Type that's raised liberal eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, telling us to arrange these letters in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of a liberal oddball who has been promoted or brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a kind of person but is printing type; 'eccentric' rearranges LIBERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The reading system for blind people uses patterns of raised dots, a kind of embossed type.

clue.text: Mastery? It's linked to sole labourer

parts.note: the upper of a shoe is the part stitched to the sole
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that skill is somehow tied to a solitary worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' suggests alone, but it is the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the advantage or control in a contest is to be in a position of dominance.

clue.text: British band in place of relief

definitions.meaning: a Britpop group from Manchester led by the Gallagher brothers
a fertile watered spot in a desert, offering respite to travellers

explanation.surface: A British band playing somewhere offering relief, like a festival rest area.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert spring is a figurative refuge, and it also names a famous 1990s Britpop group.

clue.text: Blooming appearance first giving concern

indicators.note: first places the word for appearance ahead of the word for blooming

parts.note: a look is someone's appearance
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: A flourishing appearance that worries someone at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English "that's your own lookout" means "that's your concern".
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase "that's your lookout" means it is your responsibility or affair.

clue.text: Aged relative beset by tax is nomadic type

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the tax goes around the old relative

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax
gran is grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly relative hounded by taxes ends up wandering homeless.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant wanders without a settled home, so is a roving, nomadic person.

clue.text: Habit one cop developed around hotel — revealing a fear of PCs?

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the hotel letter
developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A police officer develops a habit that shows a phobia, perhaps of police constables.
explanation.walkthrough: PCs here are personal computers, though the cop in the surface makes them police constables. HABITONECOP rearranged surrounds H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread of technology, computers included, is the meaning of this word for aversion to modern devices.

clue.text: Embrace northern type almost breaking old record

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the record is split to hold the other letters

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record, an old format

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a class is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Someone from the north, nearly breaking an old record, gets a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp something within your arms is to hug or hold it tightly.

clue.text: Interim post reviewed, one held by doctor

indicators.note: reviewed suggests being looked at again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
held by means the doctor encloses the single letter

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner
a means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A temporary job is reconsidered, with one person kept on by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges POST; a GP is a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary measure filling in until something permanent is found.

clue.text: Quiet judge in contest snubbed Latin criminal — showing discrimination?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: snubbed suggests cut short, like a snub nose, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a referee judges a sporting contest

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quiet official snubs a Latin offender, which seems like bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' trims the last E from REFEREE; 'criminal' rearranges LATIN to NTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating some more favourably than others is discrimination, which is what favouritism shows.

clue.text: Police employee US writer caught out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for caught is left out of the writer's name

parts.note: Raymond Chandler, American crime novelist
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A police worker catches out an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote the Philip Marlowe detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A police dog handler is a staff member who works with and controls a police dog.

clue.text: Wise figure keeping to right for reservation?

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the wise figure contains the other letters

parts.note: a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A wise person keeps right, perhaps showing caution or holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservation' looks like doubt or a booking, but means keeping things in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping goods in reserve for later is a form of warehousing, putting things by.

clue.text: At the right time or at a former time touring university?

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the word for formerly goes around the letter

parts.note: once means formerly

explanation.surface: Asking whether a visit to a university happened punctually or long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering on the prompt is punctual, so the phrase means exactly when expected.

clue.text: Peer introducing invention, not a noted thinker

parts.note: aristo is informal for an aristocrat, a peer

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is removed

parts.note: a tale is a story, an invention

explanation.surface: A lord brings in a new invention, though he is no famous thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes the A from TALE, leaving TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato, is among the most celebrated thinkers in history.

clue.text: Current university expelling amateur in woolly academic grouping

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in means the reduced university goes inside the woolly word

parts.note: woolly means vague or fuzzy

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so a letter is removed from the university

parts.note: Yale is a US university

explanation.surface: A university expels an amateur during a vague period, as if from a college news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'university' first suggests U, but here it is a named American university; 'Current' is not topical but electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of eight elite north-eastern US universities is an athletic conference and academic grouping.

clue.text: One in union network gets farming task

parts.note: a husband is one partner in a marriage
RY is short for railway, a network

explanation.surface: A trade union member uses networking to land a job on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The care and breeding of crops and animals is farming work, as in animal husbandry.

clue.text: His aim's cooking eastern dish

indicators.note: cooking means faking or altering, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the s is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: A chef aims to prepare a dish from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that this dish is raw, so is not cooked at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin slices of raw fish are a Japanese delicacy, a dish from the Far East.

clue.text: A promotion of flat with prominent feature — electrical feature?

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion lifts the word upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: a pad is a flat, home or lodging
a tor is a rocky peak, prominent on a moor

explanation.surface: Advertising a flat with a striking feature, like an estate agent's listing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'promotion' raises PAD to read DAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug fitting that lets a device connect to a different socket is an electrical accessory.

clue.text: Cross protected by choir at evensong

indicators.note: protected by means sheltered within, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A cross, perhaps a crucifix, sheltered by the choir at evening service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the Christian symbol, fitting the church scene, but means angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross is being angry, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Warriors with no good expressions primarily encroach

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Fighters with useless expressions mainly invade territory.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPI is a Zulu army or regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude on something or have an effect on it is to encroach upon it.

clue.text: A defensive mistake admitted by college in regretful explanation

indicators.note: admitted by means let in, so the mistake goes inside the college

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a British college
an OG is an own goal, a defender's error in football

explanation.surface: A college admits a defensive blunder in a contrite statement.
explanation.walkthrough: A polytechnic was a type of British higher-education college; OG is an own goal in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying sorry while explaining what went wrong is an expression of regret.

clue.text: Singer grasping feature that's distinctive in travel concession

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so the singer holds the other letters

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
a USP is a unique selling point, a product's distinctive feature

explanation.surface: A singer with a distinctive feature gets cheap travel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, older people and others get free or cheap bus travel with a special pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A card giving free or reduced fares on buses is a concession for travellers.

clue.text: Get rid of stunted vegetation

definitions.meaning: to cancel or abandon, as with plans

explanation.surface: Clear away scraggy undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to cancel something and land covered with stunted bushes.

clue.text: See in old squalid place milk

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: in means the word for see goes inside the squalid place

parts.note: a pit is a dirty, squalid place
lo is an old word for see or behold

explanation.surface: Seeing milk in a filthy old place, as if in a run-down dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' looks like the drink, but is a verb meaning take advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone is to take unfair advantage of them, or extract all you can.

clue.text: Ace, say, initially always valuable in alarming tennis opponents? Rather

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.words: always valuable in alarming tennis opponents? Rather

explanation.surface: An ace, a tennis winner, is always valuable when facing frightening opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' suggests tennis, but here means a flying ace; 'say' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying ace is an expert fighter pilot, an example of an airman.

clue.text: New star missing India entering Indian territory in narrow boat

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the pieces go into the territory

parts.note: Goa is a state in India

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the star

parts.note: an idol is a star or celebrity
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A new celebrity, absent from India, sails into Goa on a slender boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Goa is a small state on India's west coast, once Portuguese; 'missing' removes the letter that India stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: The long, slim Venetian rowing boat is a narrow vessel propelled by one oar.

clue.text: Mild supplier in diminutive form?

parts.note: mild is a type of beer, so a small-scale maker of beer is a little supplier of it

explanation.surface: A gentle supplier, small in size, perhaps a modest shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a dark, lightly hopped British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brewery making craft beers is literally a tiny producer of ales like mild.
